name: sqlite-insert-select
algorithm: On an in-memory sqlite database: n rows (id, a 16-byte text) inserted in one transaction through one prepared statement, then n point selects by primary key in the order id = (k * 7919) mod n + 1; the checksum is the sum of each selected id and its text's length (README.md).

skip.rust: no sqlite in Rust's std (rusqlite is a crate; no crate stands in)
skip.go: no sqlite in Go's std (database/sql has no driver; mattn/go-sqlite3 is cgo)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum cannot overflow i64 at these sizes; the task has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares a library binding; the rows read back are checked by the checksum
notes: No standard library of C, Rust, Zig or Go has sqlite, so the row compares Mk's std.db.sqlite with C calling the same amalgamation: what it measures is the wrapper, the VFS, std.libc and the process-wide lock, not sqlite.

C column: the amalgamation with its own OS layer (os_win.c) and the static C runtime's malloc. Its sqlite flags are the Mk column's, one for one, except SQLITE_OS_OTHER (the OS layer is what differs) and SQLITE_MALLOCSIZE, which names each side's own block-size call (_msize; std.libc's malloc_usable_size), so neither side keeps sqlite's 8-byte size prefix. Both compile the amalgamation without builtins and without sqlite's intrinsics (-fno-builtin here; -ffreestanding -fno-builtin from the driver there; SQLITE_DISABLE_INTRINSIC on both), at -O3 and -march=x86-64-v2 (the Mk CSource passes -march itself, since the driver gives C jobs no --cpu), so the amalgamation is compiled alike and the row measures the wrapper, the VFS, std.libc and the lock (SQL-3). Mk column: the package's CSource flags of status/std-sqlite.md (D-334), with std.libc and vfs.mk under it.

Not loadable yet: the amalgamation is outside the repository (DD-8), and tools/bench has no way to copy it into a build. The "vendor" field is the request (status/std-sqlite.md): copy files from $MK_EVIDENCE/<dir> into the mk package's build copy and compile the C column with them and c_flags. Until tools/bench reads it, the field makes this row load as broken, which tools/bench lists and sets aside.
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
